title: Keep the catalog usable during a Shipping outage
scenario: Primary Shipping can become unavailable. Test how the shop can still provide delivery information.
why: Customers need usable delivery information. Stock checks must still work when Shipping fails.
reproduce: Record a healthy baseline and your hypothesis, then disconnect Primary Shipping.
assignment: Can you restore delivery information during a primary Shipping outage?

fields.label: Healthy baseline and metric
fields.prompt: Record healthy stock, delivery information and relevant Grafana readings.

fields.label: Hypothesis and fault injection
fields.prompt: How should the system behave in case of a shipping outage? What would disprove your hypothesis?

fields.label: Fault evidence
fields.prompt: Compare stock and delivery results for all products. Record Shipping failures and fallback activity in Grafana.

fields.label: Mitigation and reason
fields.prompt: Keep the outage active. Test Shipping fallback. Optionally compare the breaker. Explain what customers regain and what remains different.

fields.label: Same-fault validation
fields.prompt: Keep the fault and traffic unchanged. Test whether your protection keeps customer results within the limits in your hypothesis. Compare with your baseline and record the evidence.

fields.label: Conclusion and cleanup
fields.prompt: Did you find a weakness? What improved, and what remains limited? Clear faults, restore defaults and verify recovery.

solution: During the outage, Refresh availability still returns stock. Refresh shipping info fails until Shipping fallback is enabled.
Shipping fallback calls a separate carrier and returns data for all three products: €4.90 and 5 days, compared with €4.90 and 3 days normally.
The breaker can pause primary calls for five seconds while backup quotes continue. But it is not necessary for this challenge.
Reconnect Primary Shipping, restore defaults and refresh to verify normal stock and delivery information.
